tossups.text: An iron catalyst named a person with this last name and Chen can oxidize inert methylene bonds. This color precedes graphene in a nickname of boron nitride nanosheets. Light of this color is produced by UV LEDs used with phosphors. Sparks of this color are seen in the flame test for magnesium metal. The background of the bottom section of the NFPA diamond is this color. Titanium dioxide is found in paint of this color, surfaces of which reflect all incident light. For 10 points, identify this color whose namesake noise is a heterogeneous mixture of sound.

In one work titled after this man, Mercury gives Robert Morris a bag of gold, Minerva stands beside an electric generator, and Ceres sits on a McCormick reaper. In that work, this title figure sits enthroned above a depiction of Freedom wearing a red, white, and blue helmet. Constantino Brumidi painted a fresco in the Capitol about this man's Apotheosis, and a painting of him was defaced when a picture of the 9/11 attacks was glued to it. In that painting of this figure, a man in green kicks aside a chunk of ice, while many boats full of horses and Revolutionary soldiers row onward in the background. For 10 points, identify this man whom Emanuel Leutze painted Crossing the Delaware on his way to the Battle of Trenton.

This substance is stopped when thrombin converts fibrinogen molecules into fibrin. Sickle cell anemia occurs due to a mutation in hemoglobin, which is carried by this substance through venules and capillaries. Platelets help this substance "clot," and it is pumped out of the aorta and through arteries and veins as it carries oxygen through the body. For 10 points, name this red fluid found in humans.

Page and Ceilker used a quantum decision process to determine the measurement procedure of this, while Saulnier and Frisch used ballistic motion to measure it. In the first experiment to calculate it, a small ball was placed to the outside of a larger ball within an isolating box, with the entire apparatus inside a barn with an opening for a telescope. The telescope observed the point when the torsion of the rope equaled the attraction between the two lead balls. For 10 points, name this constant measured by the Cavendish experiment that controls the weakest of the fundamental forces.

Michelangelo gifted Tommaso de' Cavalieri a set of four artworks in this medium, one of which shows horses tumbling in the title Fall of Phaeton. Artworks in this medium, which are housed in the Gabinetto of the Uffizi ("oo-FEET-see"), include Verocchio's Head of a Woman. During the paragone debate of the quattrocento ("KWAH-troh-CHEN-toh"), Florentine artists who emphasized a train named for the Italian word for this medium opposed the colorito associated with Titian. Works in this medium often served as modelli for paintings. Large scale works in this medium are called cartone. An artwork in this medium illustrates principles from De Architectura about human proportion by using a circle and square to bound two superimposed images of a standing man above mirror writing. For 10 points, Leonardo da Vinci's Vitruvian Man is what type of artwork, which are done with chalk or charcoal on paper?

this structure is essential for posterior pituitary hormones. It plays a key role in the endocrine system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this hypothalamus-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The hypothalamus is a key component of the Endocrine system, involved in posterior pituitary hormones.

tossups.text: In one of this man's short stories, a party thrown by Meatball Mulligan awakens Callisto, who has been nursing a bird back to health with her body heat. In one of his later novels, Prairie Wheeler searches for her mother Frenesi while her father Zoyd jumps through plate glass every year in order to prove he is insane. This man's first published short story collection was entitled Slow Learner, and his story "Under the Rose" contains characters such as Porpentine and Hugh Bongo-Shaftsbury, both of whom would later reappear in a novel about Herbert Stencil's search for the titular mysterious woman. Oedipa Maas becomes the executor of Pierce Inverarity's estate in a more famous novella by this writer, while Tyrone Slothrop attempts to evade the V2 rockets in his most famous work. For 10 points, identify this author of Mason & Dixon, V., The Crying of Lot 49, and Gravity's Rainbow.

One of these devices contains a component composed of eighteen hexagonal segments made out of gold-plated beryllium. Another one of these devices corrected for a 4-micron manufacturing error with the COSTAR system. Both of those devices use Cassegrain mounting. These non-biological devices are subject to comas, astigmatisms, and chromatic aberrations. One of these devices captured images of Westerlund 2 and the Pillars of Creation, and that device will soon be replaced by another one of them named for James Webb. For 10 points, name these optical devices used to look at stars, the most famous of which is named after Edwin Hubble.

The father of this man's rival crushed a life-size metal statue of this man with his bare hands in grief. During a quest for a fragrant flower, this man came across an old monkey whose tail he was unable to lift. A rival of this person poisoned his food and threw him in a river, but the bites of serpents in the river counteracted the poison, saving this man's life. While working as a cook, this person disguised himself in his wife's clothes in a dark room to entice a minister who had assaulted her, after which he ground that man's body into a ball of flesh. This man was called "wolf-bellied" because as a child, he gluttonously ate half of his family's meals, which led to his demise on a trek up a mountain to heaven. The arrogant thigh-slapping of this man's archrival prompted this man to kill him with an illegal blow to the thigh during a duel; that archrival was Duryodhana, the eldest of a hundred princes all killed by this man. For 10 points, name this brother of Yudhisthira and Arjuna, the second-oldest Pandava.

In human anatomy, this structure is essential for arteries vs veins vs capillaries. It plays a key role in the cardiovascular system and is one of the most studied parts of human anatomy. For ten points, name this aorta-related structure.
tossups.explanation: The aorta is a key component of the Cardiovascular system, involved in arteries vs veins vs capillaries.

tossups.text: This adjective titles a 2006 novel in which Olanna sleeps with Richard to get revenge for her boyfriend Odenigbo's infidelity just before the Biafran War. This adjective titles a story in which the narrator finds a "smooch" on the wall that fits her shoulder perfectly. In that story titled for this adjective, the narrator throws a key "down by the front steps," where it lands under a plantain leaf. In that story, the narrator begins to "smell" this color by moonlight before biting her chained-down bed and crawling around the floor. A Charlotte Perkins Gilman narrator hallucinates a woman trapped in wallpaper of-for 10 points-what title colour?

When converting from spherical to Cartesian coordinates, z is the only coordinate that does not contain this function in its definition. When writing a complex number in polar coordinates, this function is used to determine its imaginary part. Unlike its derivative, the Taylor series of this function utilizes the odd powers of x. An eponymous law relates the side lengths and this function of the angles, though that law may produce an ambiguous case. The derivative of this function is the cosine function. Name this function, which can be defined in a right triangle as opposite over hypotenuse.

One artist with this surname depicted a soldier in fatigues under a sky bursting with stars as seen through the titular Night Vision, and painted a low-key candidate walking toward a microphone against a sea of yellow-hued onlookers in Man From Boston. Howard Pyle taught an artist with this surname, also shared by a man who showed a leaf blowing in at right through an open window as a nude blond with braids grasps the edges of her stool in Lovers. That tempera enthusiast often painted the Tenants Harbor lighthouse and created 247 images of a woman sitting on or lying nude in a bed in a series of drawn for years without the knowledge of his wife, centering on Helga Testorf. That father of the aforementioned Jamie painted a work in which a pair of tracks approach a distant house and barn as the titular member of the Olson family, clad in a pink dress, stares out from a patch of grass. For 10 points, name this family of American artists that included the painter of Christina's World, Andrew.

In a scene in this film's opening, a winding staircase fades to white to reveal a bombed-out cathedral. That scene begins with blood draining back into a character's bleeding nose, followed by the camera zooming into the character's pupil. A man in this film asks his wife to cook two rabbits, which he took from a young man whose face he smashed with a wine bottle. A girl in this film eats two grapes, which awakens a monster that puts its eyeballs into the palms of its hands. That girl escapes the pale man and follows a magical stick insect to this film's title place, where she is later shot by her stepfather, Captain Vidal. A faun gives that girl, Ofelia, instructions to become princess of the underworld. For 10 points, name this Guillermo del Toro film set in Franco's Spain.

On the right side of this painting, a woman holds out a pink cloak to cover this painting's title figure. On the left side of this painting, Zephyrus, the god of wind, blows the title figure of this painting to shore. This painting's central figure stands on a floating seashell after rising from the sea. For 10 points, name this painting depicting the origin of the Roman goddess of beauty, painted by Sandro Botticelli.

A 2008 translation of this book into Dutch by Kader Abdolah added a chapter in which the central character dies. This book's influence was charted in a 2014 "Biography" by Bruce Lawrence. Thomas Carlyle described this book as "wearisome confused jumble, crude, incondite" on reading a translation by George Sale. A notable translation of this book was made by Marmaduke Pickthall. The Masnavi is often referred to as the Persian equivalent of this book. M. Mir described how this book completes the stories of Abraham, Adam and Lot, but does so only to illustrate thematic points apart from the story of Joseph in its 12th chapter. For 10 points, name this book in 114 chapters, the holy text of Islam.

This group's traditional ideas are philosophically interpreted in the book Quaestiones et Solutiones. An essay about this group argues that "political emancipation" is counterproductive for "human emancipation" and responds to a Bruno Bauer essay of the same title. Perspectives on this group represent a "comprehensive attitude... toward man in general" according to a Jean-Paul Sartre essay. An 1848 essay on the materialist view of history considers the "secular basis" for this group's religion; that Marx essay is titled for their namesake "Question." Their influence on music was blasted in an essay by Richard Wagner. For 10 points, name this religious group to whom a "Final Solution" was proposed by Adolf Hitler.

Philip Ball hypothesized that one of these events caused the Ordovician-Silurian extinction. The BATSE experiment at the Compton observatory intended to study these phenomena and provided evidence of their isotropy. The "short" variety of these events are believed to be caused by the merger of binary neutron stars in a kilonova, while their "long" types are thought to be either caused by the core collapse of Wolf-Rayet stars or hypernovae. These events, which were first detected by the Vela satellites, are followed by an "afterglow" of longer wavelength radiation. These events are considered to be the most energetic and luminous events since the Big Bang. For 10 points name these immensely energetic explosions named for the high frequency radiation they emit.

In this piece's first movement, cellos play wide E major arpeggios underneath a swelling theme by strings and clarinet. That theme is introduced at this piece's start with brass playing the fortissimo notes "E, down to B, D [pause] C B C." This piece's finale depicts a ship smashing into a cliff surmounted by a bronze statue. This work's second movement is about a noble who becomes a Sufi mystic named The Kalendar Prince. Shahryar is represented in the opening statement of "The Sea and Sinbad's Ship" in this piece, whose finale depicts "The Festival at Baghdad." For 10 points, name this orchestral suite by Nikolai Rimsky-Korsakov that depicts stories told by the protagonist of The 1,001 Nights.

A technique that analyzes the results of this process looks for a peak corresponding to a higher mass after using ethyl methanesulfonate in the first step. In some cases, after this process occurs, PCNA is ubiquitinated and an enzyme labeled with the letters eta or zeta is used in a process known as translesion synthesis. Artificially causing this process is done in TILLING and can be done in a site-directed manner. When the rate of individual events of this process occurring is constant, the molecular clock can be used to determine when two groups of life forms diverged. Pyrimidine dimers are formed when this process occurs due to ultraviolet light exposure. Insertions or deletions can result in the "frameshift" type of this process, and the "point" type affects a single nucleotide. For 10 points, name this process, the alteration of the genome of an organism.

parts.text: Name these particles, of which there are six flavors, that constitute baryons and mesons.
This physicist coined the term quark and proposed the concept of strangeness. This man also developed a method for organizing subatomic particles called the Eightfold Way.
The second generation of quarks includes the strange quark and this quark, which was predicted by the GIM mechanism. This quark was discovered in 1974 in the J/psi meson.

bonuses.leadin: The magnitude of their electric charge is either negative two-thirds or positive one-third. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this opera whose second act contains the "Song of the Golden Calf." Marguerite admires herself in the mirror during this opera's aria "Ah! je ris de me voir," also known as the "Jewel Song."

Charles Gounod originally wrote Faust as an opera comique, but it morphed into this genre of opera with large casts and spectacular designs. Giacomo Meyerbeer's Robert le Diable is representative of this genre.

Another popular operatic version of Goethe's Faust isArrigo Boito's Mefistofele. Boito also wrote the libretti for this composer's operas Falstaff and Otello. He worked with Francesco Maria Piave on his "middle period" operas like Rigoletto.

bonuses.leadin: The Paris Opera rejected this work until a fifth act ballet was inserted, because it wasn't "showy" enough. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This two-dimensional quadrilateral has two parallel sides though not necessarily two pairs of parallel sides.
This three-dimensional type of sphere or dome contains many triangles on its surface and many great circles going around it. A famous example is Spaceship Earth at EPCOT Center.
This four-dimensional analog of a square is built out of eight cubes.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, identify these shapes.

parts.text: First discovered through genetic analysis of tumor causing viruses, this is the general category of genes that when upregulated or overexpressed participate in tumorigenesis.

One of the first oncogenes discovered was a part of this superfamily of genes that encode GTPases that regulate signals involved in cellular proliferation and metastasis. Cancer-causing mutations often involve stabilization of GTP over the GDP form.

A large number of familial cases of breast cancers is thought to be derived from functional loss of this gene on chromosome 17, whose protein product is involved in DNA repair. Among others, it interacts with Susan Ferrari's favorite protein, Rad51.

bonuses.leadin: Answer these questions related to the genetics of cancer For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this instrument, which Olatunji played on We Insist!, an album by its player Max Roach. Roach pioneered bebop styles on this instrument by using a four-beat pulse on the ride cymbal rather than the bass.

The opening track on We Insist! uses this time signature to depict the whip of a slave driver. Paul Desmond wrote a song in this time signature for the album Time Out, which became the best-selling jazz single ever.

The slavery-themed lyrics of We Insist! were written by a lyricist with this surname. Roach led a quintet alongside a trumpeter of this surname, who was eulogized in Benny Golson's song "I Remember Clifford."

bonuses.leadin: One of the first major world music albums was Babatunde Olatunji's 1959 album titled for "[these instruments] of Passion." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with blood types and rh factor.
What is the main function of the erythrocyte in the cardiovascular system?
Name another component of the cardiovascular system related to blood types and rh factor.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human cardiovascular system.

parts.text: Name this English Romantic poet who was a revolutionary in the Greek War of Independence and wrote the satirical poem Don Juan [joo-un].
The four-word title of this Byron poem is followed by "like the night/Of cloudless climes and starry skies."

Byron wrote a narrative poem about François Bonivard titled for one of [these people] "of Chillon." In Alexandre Dumas's The Count of Monte Cristo, Edmond Dantès is sentenced to be one of these people in the Château d'If.

bonuses.leadin: Caroline Lamb famously referred to this poet as "mad, bad, and dangerous to know." For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this law from magnetostatics that states that the magnetic field flowing around a closed is proportional to the current enclosed by the loop. The displacement current was appended to this equation to fix it in the case of changing electric fields.

Ampère's [ahm-PEARS] law is one of the four electromagnetic equations named for this Scottish physicist. This physicist also co-names the distribution of particle velocity in an ideal gas with Ludwig Boltzmann.

When one cannot use Ampère's Law to find the magnetic field, one can use this doubly-eponymous equation instead. This equation states that the magnetic field is directly proportional to the current over the square of the distance from the wire.
acceptableAnswers: since that generalizes Biot-Savart to non-steady currents

bonuses.leadin: This law's differential form states that the curl of a B-field is equal to the permeability of free space times the current density. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this sister of Joukahainen (YO-cuh-HIGH-nin) courted by the hero Vainamoinen (VAY-nuh-MOY-nin). Rather than marry him, she drowns herself, later becoming a mermaid whom Vainamoinen catches while fishing.

Vainamoinen has difficulty getting this type of tree to grow until five women and a giant burn grass to enrich the soil; he then cuts it down because it blocks the sun. Later, he is healed by a balm made from this type of tree.
The adventures of Vainamoinen are recorded in the Kalevala, an epic from this nation compiled by Elias Lonnrot whose other sections feature Lemminkainen (lem-in-KAI-nin) and Kullervo (koo-LEHR-voh).

bonuses.leadin: When this woman tells her mother she does not want to get married, her mother advises her to spend a year eating only butter, a year eating only bacon, and a year eating only desserts. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name the primary structure associated with gallbladder and bile.
What is the main function of the liver in the digestive system?
Name another component of the digestive system related to gallbladder and bile.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points each, answer these questions about the human digestive system.

parts.text: Name this title, which is shared by a realist collection of nearly one hundred novels and short stories by Honoré de Balzac.

Balzac's gritty realism sharply contrasted with this then-popular literary movement which emphasized emotions and often included fantastical events. This movement was itself a reaction against the logic of the Enlightenment.

Balzac turned to naturalism in this novel, one of his last. In this novel, the Baron Hulot poisons Valerie and her second husband and ex-lover Crevel, in a scheme orchestrated by Hulot's distant relative, the title character.

bonuses.leadin: William Saroyan wrote a 1943 novel with this title set in Ithaca and loosely based on the Odyssey. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Identify this theory postulated by Einstein that the speed of light in a vacuum is the same in all inertial frames, regardless of the observer or the velocity of the source of light. It's contrasted with a "general" counterpart.

This effect predicted by special relativity results in the time interval measured by an observer moving with respect to a clock being longer than the measurement done by a stationary observer with respect to the clock.
A metric named for this man gives the relativistic generalization of a metric named for Euclid. He's also the namesake of a four-dimensional construct within which special relativity is set.

bonuses.leadin: 17. Some calculations within this construct involve the use of the Lorentz factor. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This architect's obsession with the color white can be seen in his recently completed Rothschild Tower located in Tel Aviv. He may be better known for his design of Los Angeles's Getty Center.
This architect placed windows of varying sizes at seemingly random locations on the white exterior of his design for the Notre Dame du Haut in Ronchamp, France.

Jorn ["yorn"] Utzøn utilized white and cream tiles for the shell-shaped exterior of one of these buildings in Sydney. Zaha Hadid created one of these buildings in Guangzhou whose exterior resembles a rock face.

bonuses.leadin: Name some things about the color white in architecture. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this genre. Carl Maria von Weber wrote two pieces, in F minor and E-flat major, for clarinet in this genre. The most famous work for clarinet in this genre was written for Anton Stadler.
That clarinet concerto was written by this "Classical" composer just weeks before he died at the age of 35. The last of his forty-one symphonies is nicknamed "Jupiter."

The tunes of the first movements of several of Mozart's works in A major, including the clarinet concerto, clarinet quintet, and twenty-third piano concerto, begin with these two notes. Please say them in the order in which they come in the piece.

bonuses.leadin: The early 19th century Finnish composer Bernhard Crusell is known for his three works for clarinet in this genre. For 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this art movement that inspired another artist's depictions of a water garden in Giverny. That artist was able to settle in Giverny due to the success of their depictions of haystacks at different times of day painted in this style.
This French artist painted several depictions of water lilies in their garden at Giverny. This artist's painting of a sunrise lent its name to the Impressionist art movement.
Monet's garden included a footbridge inspired by those in this country, whose ukiyo-e prints inspired many Impressionist artists. Hokusai's Great Wave off Kanagawa depicts this country's Mount Fuji.

bonuses.leadin: The village of Giverny was home to a colony of American artists practicing this style's "Decorative" form. For 10 points each:

parts.text: These texts, used in Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism, are a series of short aphorisms meant to be easily memorized. The name of these texts is the Sanskrit word for "thread."
The daily recitation of passages from the Guru Granth Sahib(gu-ROO grunt SAH-hib) is a key practice of this religion. The Guru Granth Sahib is considered the eleventh and final guru of this religion.
A hafiz (HAH-fizz) or hafiza(HAH-fi-za) is one who has memorized the entirety of this religious text. This is the central holy book of Islam.

bonuses.leadin: For 10 points, answer the following about the memorization of religious texts:

parts.text: Name this thinker, who used the argument from marginal cases and principle of equal consideration to argue certain beings deserved rights in a 1975 book.

The principle of equal consideration, which Singer used to argue for animal rights, is based on this ethical theory founded by Jeremy Bentham that prioritizes achieving the greatest happiness for the greatest number.

Peter Singer's book The Most Good You Can Do argues in favor of a contemporary movement named for the "effective" form of this concept that proposes using science and reason to benefit as many people as possible.

bonuses.leadin: This thinker claimed that there is no moral difference between saving a drowning child or a Bengali person ten thousand miles away in his essay "Famine, Affluence, and Morality." For 10 points each:

parts.text: The Leclanché cell contains an anode made of this element with symbol Zn.
At the anode, zinc is oxidized to this oxidation state, which is also the preferred oxidation state of magnesium.

Like all galvanic cells, Leclanché cells have one of these structures that prevent the entire cell from rapidly reaching equilibrium. These structures work by connecting two half-cells and are made of glass or filter paper.

bonuses.leadin: Answer the following about the Leclanché cell, for 10 points each:

parts.text: Name this Australian composer and pianist, renowned for his arrangements of English folk songs such as Country Gar-dens and Shepherd's Hey.

Grainger trolled performers by including time signatures of 2.5/4 and 1.5/4, and by making the woodwinds play sextu-plets, in the "Lord Melbourne" and "Brisk Young Sailor" movements of this collection of folk songs for concert band.
Grainger's piece In Dahomey pays tribute to black American folk music, something that this Czech composer also did in his E minor ninth symphony.

bonuses.leadin: The choral work To a Nordic Princess was composed for the Hollywood Bowl wedding of this composer to Ella Str¨om, a poor girl who had no idea about his sadomasochistic fetishes. For 10 points each:

parts.text: This lobe of the brain is involved in decision making and recognizing the consequences of potential actions. It is anterior to the parietal lobe.

This area is one of the two areas of the brain traditionally recognized as being involved with speech. In its namesake aphasia, also called receptive aphasia, language comprehension is impaired and speech is fluent but meaningless.

This pathway, which connects the frontal cortex to part of the temporoparietal junction, was previously thought to connect Wernicke's area to Broca's area. Damage to this pathway can cause conduction aphasia.

bonuses.leadin: Name some areas of the brain, for 10 points each.
